narratives.Description: bug(session,occupancy): payload-identity hosts mint a UUID lease on claim, so session:start/ready locks the session out of its own worktree
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

On every host whose identity contract is `payload`-sourced — `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, i.e. three of the four supported hosts — `deft session:start` / `session:ready` claims the worktree lease under a freshly minted UUID instead of the host-published owner. The hook then presents the host identity, does not match the lease, and denies every write. The session is locked out of the worktree it just armed, by its own claim.

This is deterministic, not a race, and `occupancy.ts` already documents it as the failure mode the host step exists to prevent.

## Mechanism

`packages/core/src/session/host-session-owner.ts:29`:

```ts
const HOST_IDENTITY_SOURCES: Readonly<Record<HookHostIdentityProvider, HookHostIdentitySource>> = {
  codex:  { kind: "payload",  field: "session_id" },
  claude: { kind: "payload",  field: "session_id" },
  cursor: { kind: "payload",  field: "conversation_id" },
  grok:   { kind: "host-env", variable: "GROK_SESSION_ID" },
};
```

`HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_ENTRIES` filters that table to `kind === "host-env"`, so it resolves to **grok only**. `ambientHostSessionOwner()` iterates exactly those entries, so on claude / codex / cursor it always returns `null`.

That is the host step of `resolvePresentedIdentity`, which `resolveOccupancySessionId` depends on. With no explicit `--session-id` and no `DEFT_SESSION_ID` in the environment, the chain falls through to the mint at `occupancy.ts:651`. The comment immediately above it states the consequence:

> The host step is what makes an identified host's claim reachable (#3873). Minting instead binds the lease to an id no later hook process can present, so the session that claimed the worktree is refused by its own lease. The mint stays as the last resort for hosts that publish nothing.

Claude Code is not a host that publishes nothing. It publishes `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` in the CLI process environment, and that value is exactly what the hook presents:

```
$ echo $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
3d367ca0-6f5d-4152-82fe-31b3b8ff8de6

$ printf '%s' "3d367ca0-6f5d-4152-82fe-31b3b8ff8de6" | base64 -w0
M2QzNjdjYTAtNmY1ZC00MTUyLTgyZmUtMzFiM2I4ZmY4ZGU2

hook denial presented: host:claude:v1:M2QzNjdjYTAtNmY1ZC00MTUyLTgyZmUtMzFiM2I4ZmY4ZGU2
```

The identity is sitting in the environment the claim path already reads. It is skipped because the provider table declares `claude` as payload-only, and `HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_ENTRIES` has no entry for it.

## Reproduction

Claude Code desktop, v0.116.0, Windows 11.

1. From the primary checkout, hit compaction staleness (`session ritual state is stale (older than 4h)`). Both printed recoveries refuse on the primary checkout — this is #4290.
2. Take the sanctioned escape: `git worktree add .deft-scratch/worktrees/<slug> -b chore/<slug>`.
3. In the worktree, run `deft session:ready`. It succeeds:

```
occupancy claimed session 98c1c5a7-79ca-4c9e-9b88-447456b9b0b9 (intent=mutation)
OK session ready (gated ritual verified).
```

4. Attempt any write. Denied:

```
Directive denied Write: Worktree occupied by session 98c1c5a7-79ca-4c9e-9b88-447456b9b0b9
(intent=mutation, heartbeat 31s ago, no recorded write, ...).
This process presented session host:claude:v1:M2QzNjdjYTAtNmY1ZC00MTUyLTgyZmUtMzFiM2I4ZmY4ZGU2,
which neither holds that lease nor has a write grant on it.
```

The lease was created seconds earlier by this same session's own `session:ready`.

## The printed recoveries do not resolve it either

The denial lists four options. Three are unusable here:

- **"Use another worktree"** — a fresh worktree reproduces it identically; the mint happens on every claim.
- **"Ask the occupant for a write grant"** — the occupant is a phantom UUID with no process behind it. Nothing can run `occupancy:grant` as it.
- **"session:start --steal --confirm"** — stealing from yourself, and #4410 is specifically about this deny text handing agents the steal recipe.

Bare `deft occupancy:release` also refuses:

```
This process presented no session identity, so a write grant cannot name it
and an owner transition would not be recognised on its next write.
```

The only escape found was to name the phantom explicitly, then re-claim as the host owner:

```bash
deft occupancy:release --session-id=98c1c5a7-79ca-4c9e-9b88-447456b9b0b9
deft session:start --session-id=host:claude:v1:M2QzNjdjYTAtNmY1ZC00MTUyLTgyZmUtMzFiM2I4ZmY4ZGU2
```

That requires the operator to read the minted UUID out of one message, the canonical host id out of another, and know that `--session-id` on `session:start` is the fix. An autonomous agent following the printed ladder in order reaches `--steal` first.

## Expected

1. Give `claude` (and `codex` / `cursor`) a `host-env` identity source alongside their payload source, so `ambientHostSessionOwner` resolves the same owner the hook will present. For Claude Code the variable is `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. The provider table already supports per-host sources; it needs dual-source entries rather than one-of.
2. Until then, `resolveOccupancySessionId` should not mint on a host that *has* a declared identity contract. Minting is documented as the last resort "for hosts that publish nothing"; claude/codex/cursor publish something, the CLI just cannot see it through the current table. Refusing with "this host publishes identity in the hook payload; re-run with `--session-id=<id>`" is better than a lease nobody can use.
3. When a claim is refused against a lease whose owner is not a canonical `host:<provider>:v1:` id and which has no recorded write, say so. The current text describes a phantom UUID in the same words it uses for a live peer, which is what sends the reader toward `--steal`.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#4290** — primary-checkout staleness with no recovery. This issue is what happens on the escape route that one recommends: the linked worktree also dead-ends, for a different reason.
- **#4410** — deny text hands an agent the steal recipe. This is a case where the steal path is the *only* one of the four printed options an agent would reach, against a lease with no process behind it.
- **#4028** — occupancy reliability tracker; likely parent.
- **#4020** — forge-only sessions that do not claim the worktree lease; adjacent posture work.
- **#3873 / #3954 / #4066** — the host step, shared lookup order, and host-authoritative claim. The mechanism here is the gap those left for payload-sourced hosts.

Seat: claude. Round 1, fresh critic. Charter refutation. Reads pinned to `23765f7d60e5b7d5ce3139d1a547c1eb68b6d68a`. Input ceiling `5639922010`, inclusive; nothing after it was read.

## Verdict on the refutation target

**The premise does not survive — but not on the ground the write-back recorded.**

The write-back's strongest-case-against is that payload-only is a deliberate control against inherited-environment identity, and that expected-item 1 would reintroduce the #4066 class. I ran that and it is inverted (finding D). Payload-only is not a control against inherited environment identity; it is what keeps the #4066 control *switched off* on `claude`.

The premise still fails, on two grounds the issue never reaches: the mechanism it says is missing already exists and is wired for exactly these three hosts (finding A), and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` fails both documented preconditions of the `host-env` kind (finding E). The issue's factual claims are all true and all verified below; its causal claim — "skipped because the provider table declares `claude` as payload-only" — is false. The table is one half of a deliberate partition, and the bug is that the other half did not reach the reported path.

## What I re-verified by running it

Executed against the pinned tree, not cited:

- `ambientHostSessionOwner(process.env)` returns `null` in a live Claude Code process. The skip is real.
- `readHostEnvIdentity(process.env, "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID")` is `ok` with `3d367ca0-6f5d-4152-82fe-31b3b8ff8de6`, and `canonicalHostSessionId("claude", …)` on it yields `host:claude:v1:M2QzNjdjYTAtNmY1ZC00MTUyLTgyZmUtMzFiM2I4ZmY4ZGU2` — byte-identical to the owner the hook presented in the body's denial.
- `resolveOccupancySessionId({env:{CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:…}})` mints. Reproduced.
- PATH probe: `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `deft`, `deft-hook` all resolve. The write-back's seat-family anchor holds.
- `HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_VARIABLES` is `["GROK_SESSION_ID"]`, and `host-session-owner.test.ts` locks that exact array.

## A — blocks-the-design: expected-item 1 proposes a mechanism that already exists, wired for exactly these three hosts

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` carries `UPDATED_INPUT_WIRE_HOSTS = ["codex", "claude", "cursor"]` and `attachLifecycleIdentityRewrite`, which resolves the payload host owner and rewrites an allowed `deft session:start` / `session:ready` to append `--session-id=host:<provider>:v1:<…>`. Its doc comment states the partition in terms: a host outside that list "binds its claim in the CLI instead: `resolveOccupancySessionId` resolves the same ambient host owner the write gate will present." `HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_ENTRIES` resolves to `grok` alone — the exact complement over `HOST_IDENTITY_PROVIDERS`. Payload hosts bind through the hook rewrite; host-env hosts bind through the CLI ambient. Two branches, one per kind.

**Failure mode.** Ship item 1 and `claude` sits in both branches at once. The hook appends an explicit `--session-id`, and `resolvePresentedIdentity` puts explicit ahead of host, so on every path the hook covers the new environment source is never consulted. It goes live only on the paths the hook does not cover — exactly the least supervised ones. A remedy whose only live effect is on the unsupervised path is not a fix to the mechanism; it is a second, unguarded authority added beside a working one.

**Disposition consequence.** Item 1 cannot bind as written. The defect statement has to be re-cut from "the provider table is wrong" to "the claim-binding bridge does not cover path X", and the remedy becomes bridge coverage.

## B — blocks-the-design: the repro's own escape route has no Directive hook registered, and the issue never names this

**Evidence.** `.claude/settings.json` in the primary checkout registers `deft-hook --host claude --event tool.before` against the `Shell|Bash|BashTool|shell|bash` matcher — that is the process that would have bridged the claim. `git ls-tree -r 23765f7d60e5b7d5ce3139d1a547c1eb68b6d68a` returns no `.claude/settings.json`: the file is untracked and exists only in the primary checkout. `.deft-scratch/worktrees/4424-root-cause` has no `.claude` directory at all.

**Failure mode.** Step 2 of the reproduction is `git worktree add .deft-scratch/worktrees/<slug>`. Because the registration is untracked, a linked worktree materialises with no Directive hook, so step 3's `deft session:ready` cannot be bridged under *any* provider-table change. Separately, the body describes the operator running the command, and an operator terminal has no PreToolUse hook by construction. Both halves of the reported repro sit outside the bridge, for reasons unrelated to `HOST_IDENTITY_SOURCES`.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean must name which of {operator terminal, unregistered linked worktree, non-inspectable command} the remedy covers. A lean that changes identity sourcing and does not answer this leaves the filed reproduction reproducing.

## C — blocks-the-design: the in-hook bridge fails open on non-inspectable commands, into the same mint

**Evidence.** `exactLifecycleInvocation` returns `null` for any command with quoting, chaining, a wrapper, or a backslash-bearing token. `inspectExactLifecycleCommand` then returns `null`, and `attachLifecycleIdentityRewrite` returns the incoming decision unchanged — an `allow` with no owner bound. Contrast the adjacent arm: when the command *is* inspectable but outside the rewrite surface, `sessionIdStatus === "absent" && !rewriteAllowed` denies with "Re-run the command with `--session-id=…`".

**Failure mode.** Inspectable-but-unsafe fails closed; non-inspectable fails open. `deft session:start && echo ok`, or the same verb under PowerShell quoting, or any path-bearing form, silently reaches `resolveOccupancySessionId`, mints, and produces the exact lockout in the body — on a fully registered checkout, with the provider table untouched.

**Disposition consequence.** This is the reported bug on a second path. Any lean that binds only an identity-sourcing change leaves it, and it will be re-filed.

## D — sharpens-framing: the write-back's strongest-case-against is directionally inverted

**Evidence.** Executed against `occupancy.ts` at the dispatch SHA:

- `grok` + inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID` → presented `source: "environment"`, `disagreeingHostOwner: "host:grok:v1:…"`, claim resolves to the **host** owner. The #4066 control fires.
- `claude` + inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID` → presented `source: "environment"`, `disagreeingHostOwner: **null**`, claim resolves to the **inherited value**. The control cannot fire.

The #4066 branch is guarded on `identity.source === "environment" && identity.disagreeingHostOwner !== null`. With no host step there is no disagreement to detect, so on `claude` the control is inert and an inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID` is taken at face value today. `DEFT_SESSION_ID` is inherited by child processes by exactly the mechanism the write-back attributes to `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and it sits *ahead* of the host step in the lookup order.

**Failure mode.** Adjudicating on the recorded counter would refuse item 1 for re-opening a class that is already open on this host, and would leave open the one path where a child *can* currently claim as its parent. Reasoning from a control that cannot execute is how a premise survives a panel.

**Disposition consequence.** The refutation target cannot be upheld on the inheritance argument as recorded. If the arc still refuses item 1 — and it should — it must refuse it on findings A and E, and the lean should say so explicitly rather than inherit the write-back's framing.

## E — blocks-the-design: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` fails both documented preconditions of the `host-env` kind

**Evidence, precondition 1 (unreachable from the agent's shell).** `host-session-owner.ts` states the kind's safety property directly: `host-env` providers publish into "the environment of the processes the host spawns… the hook is a sibling of the agent's shell rather than a descendant, so a shell export cannot reach it." For `grok`, both readers sit behind that property, so a forged export yields a claim the hook will not match and the split fails closed. For `claude` the hook would keep reading the payload, so the environment half would be read only by CLI processes that *are* descendants of the agent's shell — precisely where an export does reach. And the value is unconstrained: I ran `isUsableHostSessionId` over `not-a-uuid`, `../../etc`, and a 512-byte run; all three pass, and all three canonicalize to well-formed `host:claude:v1:…` owners that round-trip through `parseCanonicalHostSessionId`. There is no shape check and no attestation.

**Evidence, precondition 2 (a different id per agent session).** `occupancy.ts` answers parent-and-child per identity-source kind, and the host-env branch rests on a factual claim: "On a `host-env` host the parent and its dispatched children are different actors, because the host publishes a different id into each agent session." Measured inside this critic process, which is a dispatched child: `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=3d367ca0-6f5d-4152-82fe-31b3b8ff8de6` — byte-identical to the parent's, and to the raw id inside the owner the body's denial presented. The host publishes the *same* id into each agent session.

**Failure mode.** Two concrete ones. (i) `kind` stops predicting the parent/child model, so the single paragraph that answers "parent and child" becomes false for one of its two branches while nothing in it changes. (ii) `HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_VARIABLES` is documented as the surface a caller scrubs — "a hermetic test process, a dispatcher scrubbing a child's environment" — and three CLI occupancy test files scrub exactly that list. Adding the variable makes Directive's own scrubbers delete the host's live identity out of a child's environment, on a host whose children legitimately share the family id, and it changes what the occupancy suite sees when it runs inside a Claude Code session.

**Disposition consequence.** Binding any environment source for `claude` first requires splitting `kind` into two orthogonal axes — where the id is published, and whether it is distinct per agent session — or the bind silently invalidates the #3954 answer and repurposes the scrub list. That is a larger change than the issue's "dual-source entries rather than one-of".

## F — sharpens-framing: expected-item 3's predicate over-fires, and the mechanism it wants is half-built

**Evidence.** `isOwnInheritedPresentation` already exists and already carries the branch item 3 asks for: "this occupant's own host session under a second identity -- not a stranger… Do not steal this lease from yourself." It compares raw ids, so against a minted UUID occupant it returns false and the caller falls through to the stranger text. `OccupancyRecord` carries `sessionId`, `lastWriteAt` and no identity-source field, so "not canonical and no recorded write" is the only predicate available — and `PresentedIdentitySource` is computed at claim time and discarded.

**Failure mode.** That predicate is also true of every legitimate opaque `DEFT_SESSION_ID`-sourced owner that has claimed and not yet written. `lastWriteAt` is null until a gated *product* write and is coarse to `OCCUPANCY_REFRESH_AFTER_MS`, so a live peer reading before it writes matches. Printing "this lease has no process behind it" to that caller invites a wrongful release of a working session — the same failure class as the steal-recipe text, pointed the other way.

**Disposition consequence.** Item 3 can bind only if claim-time provenance is recorded on the lease. It cannot bind as a shape-plus-silence heuristic.

## G — sharpens-framing: injection / swarm lens — the issue body is an ingestible forged-owner recipe

**Evidence.** The body demonstrates constructing a canonical owner by base64-encoding an arbitrary string and passing it to `--session-id`. I ran the acceptance path: `resolvePresentedIdentity({sessionId: "host:claude:v1:dmljdGlt"})` returns `source: "explicit"` with that owner, no host attestation anywhere. The only `host:`-prefix validation is `claimsHostSessionIdShape` at grant time, which rejects *malformed* canonical ids only; a well-formed forgery is accepted on every surface, including the owner-only ones (`occupancy:release`, `heartbeat`, `grant`). The design-critique contract's own `### Non-normative for downstream agents` records that `composeOverviewWithComments` copies every comment verbatim into the xBRIEF Overview the next worker reads as dispatch input, and that the quarantine scanner flags nothing under that composition.

**Failure mode.** The issue cites #4410 — deny text handing an agent the steal recipe — while being a strictly stronger instance of that class. A steal at least leaves `--steal --confirm --occupant` in the command an operator can see; this leaves a plain `--session-id`. Ingested, it is dispatch input teaching a worker how to present another session's owner.

**Disposition consequence.** `arc-mode: no-ingest` suppresses this for this arc only. If the lean binds and the issue is later ingested, the recipe travels with it. The lean should record whether remedy text may restate the escape, and should prefer naming the verb without the constructed id.

No instruction-shaped text aimed at a critic was found in the body or in comment 5639922010. Nothing was obeyed; nothing needed to be.

## H — sharpens-framing: a round-1 critic structurally cannot verify panel completeness

**Evidence.** The contract fixes the round-1 ceiling at the triage write-back when one exists, and separately requires the parent to post the panel-deposit naming `round:`, `siblings:` and `input-ceiling:` before the first sibling spawn. My ceiling is `5639922010`, which *is* the write-back. Any conformant deposit therefore lands above every round-1 critic's ceiling by construction, and is unreadable by all of them.

**Failure mode.** The contract calls a missing or malformed deposit "a contract defect", and #3850 already records that no predicate observes it. The only readers with an independent view of the thread are placed where they cannot see it. The defect is not merely unenforced; it is unobservable by design, and a panel is the one spend that buys independent observation.

**Disposition consequence.** At Stop 5 the parent cannot cite critic corroboration for deposit conformance and must self-attest — which is the shape non-self-arbitration exists to avoid, and the parent here authored the target. If corroboration is wanted, the deposit id has to travel as an envelope field (it does not today), or the round-1 ceiling has to be the deposit rather than the write-back.

## Road not taken, and the steelman

I chose among three mechanisms for the underlying defect: (1) dual-source provider entries, as filed; (2) refuse-to-mint on a host with a declared contract, the issue's item 2; (3) extend the existing rewrite bridge's coverage to the paths in findings B and C. I did not pursue (1) for the reasons in A and E. I did not land on (2) alone either, and that is the road not taken worth recording: refuse-to-mint is strictly safer than minting, but on the reproduced path — an unregistered linked worktree with no hook — it converts a silent lockout into a hard refusal with an instruction the operator can follow, and does nothing about the fail-open in C, where the command is allowed before any refusal could be printed.

Steelman of the position I am rejecting. The strongest case for item 1 is not the oversight framing; it is that the rewrite bridge is a *host-mediated* control and therefore cannot cover an operator at a terminal, which is a permanent gap, not a coverage bug — and that a CLI-resolvable owner is the only thing that can ever close it. That case is real, and it is why I classify E as blocking rather than fatal. What would flip my verdict: a measurement showing that `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is re-minted per agent session rather than inherited — I measured the opposite in this process — or a claim path that reads it only when the hook is demonstrably absent and records that provenance on the lease, so the environment source can never outrank a payload owner that exists. Absent one of those, the environment half is a second authority with no cross-check on the only paths where it is live.
